national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said that the Indian Economy is moving ahead as the fastest-growing major economy despite warfare and instability prevailing in several parts of the world. Addressing the nation on the eve of the 80th Independence Day this evening, the President highlighted that according to economic projections, the growth rate of the Indian economy is expected to be more than twice the average global growth rate. She added that ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan’ has further strengthened the foundation of the country’s economic progress and national security. The President highlighted that India has achieved some of the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, ahead of schedule. President Droupadi Murmu also noted that national interest is the foundation of India’s foreign policy and peace, cooperation, dialogue, and the ideal of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam are the pillars of its foreign policy. She said, India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with many countries to enhance economic cooperation and strengthen mutual relations. The President said that India is playing a leading role among the countries of the Global South and the country has grown in stature on the global stage. President Murmu said, India believes in a rules-based international order, and her endeavour is to ensure that the global community receives appropriate representation in the United Nations and other multilateral organisations. She said, this endeavour has been getting strong support from many countries. On Operation Sindoor, President Droupadi Murmu said that the historic operation against terrorism demonstrated the capability of the Indian Armed Forces to act with precision. She said, the Operation sent a clear and firm message to terrorists and those who support them that no matter where they hide, they will have to face the consequences of their actions. She said, the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty with the country that harbours terrorism is a decisive step in the interest of the nation, especially the farmers. President Droupadi Murmu highlighted that making the country Naxal-free is a major achievement, as for decades, Naxalism posed a serious challenge to the nation. She said, today, the areas once affected by Naxalism are filled with enthusiasm. In her address, the President said that students are the architects of India’s future and everyone must contribute to safeguard their future. As Public examinations become gateways to the opportunities for the students, she emphasised that the Government is undertaking comprehensive steps to reform these examinations. The objectives of these reforms are to completely curb the use of unfair means in public examinations, make the examination system more transparent, more secure, and more trustworthy for the youth. President Droupadi Murmu also highlighted that equality of status and of opportunity, along with the dignity of the individual, are among the cherished ideals of the Constitution. She said, today, people from ordinary backgrounds are making extraordinary contributions in many fields. national_raw_news.title: 11 hours ago | National 44 India Reiterates Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh Are Integral Parts of the Country
national_raw_news.content: New Delhi today reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are an inalienable and integral part of India. Briefing media in the national capital this evening, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, the issues that should concern the international community are the atrocities currently being perpetrated in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, and the use of PoJK for cross-border terrorism. Replying to a question, Mr Jaiswal stated that India has had several engagements with Afghanistan in the last few months. He highlighted that there have been several Ministerial visits from Afghanistan to India, which have led to the strengthening of partnership in areas including development, cooperation, trade, and connectivity. He added that India has long-standing ties with Afghanistan, and it looks forward to further strengthening these ties. On Bangladesh requesting additional diesel supplies from India amid energy crisis, Mr Jaiswal said, India has an ongoing arrangement with Bangladesh for the supply of diesel. He added that the additional request for diesel will be examined keeping in mind India’s own requirements, refining capacity, as well as the availability of diesel in the country. Replying to another query, the spokesperson said, India has extended an invitation to Prime Minister of Bangladesh, Tarique Rahman for a bilateral visit. India has also extended an invitation to the Bangladesh PM for a visit to India for the outreach session of the BRICS Summit. On FCRA, the spokesperson reiterated that legislative matters concerning India are internal matters on which Parliament will decide. On Russian President Vladimir Putin’s statement that India is showing growing interest in Russia’s Northern Sea Route, the spokesperson pointed out that India has a multi-faceted cooperation with Russia and connectivity is an important part of this. Mr Jaiswal conveyed deepest condolences on the lives that have been lost due to the earthquake in Colombia. He said, India sent 20 metric tons of relief material to the country today, which includes medical supplies, medical equipment, and several other items that are helpful for post-earthquake recovery.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi court allows CBI to conduct further investigation in NEET-UG paper leak case
national_raw_news.content: The Special Fast Track Court in Delhi has allowed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to conduct further investigation in the NEET UG Paper leak case, as new evidence has surfaced during the investigation. The CBI sought permission to keep open the investigation into other conspirators in the NEET UG Paper leak case, other than 13 accused persons against whom a charge sheet has already been filed. Special Judge Ajay Gupta allowed the application of the CBI and said that it is well settled law that further investigation can be carried out even after commencement of trial. In its letter, the CBI stated that after analysing CFSL reports, certain digital evidence has surfaced due to which it has become necessary to obtain further expert opinions. It was also stated that some more digital devices, seized during investigation, are being sent to CFSL, and the reports of which shall be filed, as and when received. The CBI said that further investigation with regard to the involvement of other conspirators is continuing and upon completion of the same, a supplementary charge-sheet will be filed.

national_raw_news.title: NTA to release provisional answer keys for UGC-NET, CSIR-NET and ICAR-NET 2026
national_raw_news.content: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has announced that the provisional answer keys for UGC-NET, CSIR-NET and ICAR AIEEA (PG) and AICE (PhD) 2026 will be published tomorrow. The NTA advised candidates to rely only on official communications from the agency regarding the examinations and answer keys. The computer-based examination, held across 87 subjects, determines eligibility for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), appointment as Assistant Professor, and admission to PhD programmes in universities across the country. Earlier, the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students’ Union (JNUSU) wrote to the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the NTA expressing “deep concern” over the delay in releasing the provisional answer key and final results.

national_raw_news.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman says PM Internship Scheme aims to bridge industry-skill gap
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) has been designed to help bridge the gap between industry expectations and the skills of candidates who apply for jobs under the scheme. Interacting with the interns in New Delhi, Mrs Sitharaman said the scheme has been designed after interactions with industry people as well as graduates and those who completed ITI courses. Under the PMIS, implemented by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, those in the 18-25 age group are eligible to join and the interns receive a minimum financial assistance of 9,000 rupees per month. The third round of the pilot phase of the scheme is underway. The Minister said the scheme is helping bridge this gap by providing young people with hands-on industry experience. She said the scheme also enables the youth to pursue internship opportunities in areas of interest and the candidates will be able to get additional skills beyond their qualifications.

national_raw_news.title: Romania Begins Shutdown of Second Cernavoda Nuclear Reactor Amid Severe Drought
national_raw_news.content: Romania has begun a controlled shutdown of the second reactor at its Cernavoda nuclear power plant as severe drought continues to affect much of Europe. Plant operator Nuclearelectrica said scorching temperatures and weeks of below-average rainfall have pushed the Danube River to record-low levels. The conditions forced the plant to shut down its first reactor in late July this year. The plant accounts for around 20 per cent of Romania’s electricity generation when operating at full capacity. Meanwhile, the country’s Ministry of Energy has said the country’s electricity needs can be met through alternative sources and imports following the shutdown of the second reactor.

national_raw_news.title: Eight Killed in Suspected Gas Leak at Shipbreaking Yard in Bangladesh
national_raw_news.content: Eight people were killed in a suspected gas leak at a shipbreaking yard in Bangladesh today. Police said, the incident occurred at the Ferdous Steel Ship Breaking Yard in the Sitakunda area, during the dismantling of a decommissioned ship. Several other workers were injured in the incident. Police said, the initial death toll was six, but two more workers succumbed to their injuries after being taken from the site. Officials said, the workers died due to toxic gas emissions from the ship. Authorities are investigating the cause of the gas leak and whether adequate safety measures were in place for the workers at the yard.

national_raw_news.title: Two UAE vessels attacked while transiting Strait of Hormuz
national_raw_news.content: Two vessels of the United Arab Emirates were attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz last evening. In a statement posted on social media, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iranian attacks, stressing the necessity for Iran to cease attacks. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs noted that this attack constitutes a flagrant violation of UN Security Council resolution 2817, which affirmed the importance of freedom of navigation, and rejected the targeting of commercial vessels or the obstruction of international maritime routes. The Ministry stressed that targeting commercial shipping and using the Strait of Hormuz as a tool of economic coercion or blackmail represents acts of piracy by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps and constitutes a direct threat to the stability of the region, its peoples, and global energy security.

Praggnanandhaa bounced back from his previous-round defeat to secure a convincing victory over Dutch player Jorden Van Foreest in the fourth round of the Sinquefield Cup. national_raw_news.title: Iga Swiatek beats Elena Rybakina to claim Women’s Singles title at Canadian Open Tennis 14 Aug 2026 | 8:30 AM 368
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, seventh seed Iga Swiatek of Poland defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in straight sets to claim the Women’s Singles title in Toronto last night. Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2 6-3 win, giving her a confidence boost heading into the US Open. In Men’s Singles, American tennis player Ben Shelton won the title in Montreal by defeating fellow American Brandon Nakashima with a score of 6-3, 7-6(4). With this victory, the fifth-seeded Shelton successfully defended his tournament crown and captured his second career ATP Masters 1000 trophy. This victory marks his fourth tournament win of the 2026 season, following earlier titles in Dallas, Munich, and Stuttgart, bringing his total career tour-level titles to seven.

national_raw_news.title: Commonwealth Fencing: Indian team dominates with 35 medals comprising 13 gold 13 Aug 2026 | 8:30 PM 881
national_raw_news.content: India emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship by winning an impressive 35 medals after four days of competition held at Lagos in Nigeria. Indian contingent secured thirteen gold, eight silver, and fourteen bronze medals at the event across the Under 23 and senior competitions. The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth and final day of the competition, securing honours in Men’s Sabre, Women’s Sabre, Men’s E’pée, Women’s Epée and Women’s foil, as well as a silver in Men’s foil. The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results. Secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, Rajeev Mehta, said in a statement that lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s exports register robust growth of over 13% in July 13 Aug 2026 | 8:45 PM 286
national_raw_news.content: The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month. Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Manohar Lal inaugurates Har Ghar Tiranga kiosk as part of nationwide ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister Manohar Lal inaugurates Har Ghar Tiranga kiosk as part of nationwide patriotic campaign Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister Manohar Lal inaugurates Har Ghar Tiranga kiosk as part of nationwide patriotic campaign ANI | Updated: Aug 14, 2026 22:52 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 14 (ANI): Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Manohar Lal, inaugurated the Har Ghar Tiranga kiosk at the India Habitat Centre (IHC), New Delhi, as part of the nationwide Har Ghar Tiranga campaign being observed from 9th to 17th August 2026 under the aegis of the Government of India. According to a press release, the event, organised by Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited (HUDCO), a Navratna NBFC-IFC under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), was marked by patriotic fervour and enthusiasm. The Inauguration took place in the presence of Sanjay Kulshrestha, CMD, HUDCO, Prof K G Suresh, Director, IHC, Dr Vibha Dhawan, Director General, TERI, officials of HUDCO and IHC, representatives from various organisations located in the India Habitat Centre and schoolchildren. Speaking on the occasion, the Union Minister called upon citizens to participate wholeheartedly in the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign and proudly hoist the National Flag at their homes. Interacting with the children, Manohar Lal highlighted that the Tiranga is far more than a national symbol; it represents India's hard-earned freedom, unity, identity, dignity and the collective aspirations of its people. Addressing the youth, the Minister urged that they should appreciate the cost of independence that has been secured with many sacrifices and urged them to carry forward the national values and make the campaign a personal expression of patriotism, the press release stated. According to the press release the minister appreciated HUDCO's initiative to take the campaign to citizens through its offices and outreach activities, and encouraged greater public participation in making the campaign a nationwide celebration of national unity, pride and collective responsibility. As part of its commitment to contribute meaningfully to the national campaign , HUDCO will distribute over 5,000 National Flags through its kiosk at India Habitat Centre (IHC), as well as through its Regional Offices across the country. The press release further stated that the venue was adorned in the tricolour, creating an atmosphere of patriotism and festivity. Selfie points themed around the National Flag were also set up, encouraging participants to capture and share their patriotic moments under the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign . Adding to the festive spirit, children from the Habitat Learning Centre presented a soulful rendition of Vande Mataram, following which the Minister distributed National Flags among the children, inspiring them to participate in the campaign with pride and enthusiasm. People across age groups participated with great enthusiasm and proudly posed with the National Flag, expressing their joy and pride in being part of a campaign that celebrates the spirit of oneness, patriotism and national pride, the press release said. The expansion will create a 60 km network and include a planned connection to Dholera International Airport , and the Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation (GMRC) is overseeing development. Final approval from the Union Cabinet is required before civil construction may begin. A principal element of Phase Three is a corridor from Thaltej Gam to Badrabad via Godhavi that will start at Shilaj Canal Road and follow the Sardar Patel Ring Road before reaching Badrabad near the Ahmedabad-Dholera Expressway. The Badrabad terminal has been proposed as a future interchange for extensions towards the Dholera Special Investment Region and the airport , intended to enhance connectivity in south west Ahmedabad. The plan will also integrate the new corridors with the existing East?West and North?South lines to provide additional interchange options. The proposal foresees a circular corridor beginning and ending at Vadaj that will loop through western, eastern and southern parts of the city and call at key locations such as Akhbarnagar, Naranpura and Amraiwadi to offer alternatives to central city travel. Major interchanges are planned at Gujarat University, APMC, Amraiwadi and Vadaj to facilitate passenger movement without routing through the central business district. The expanded network is expected to include 41 elevated stations across the 60 km of new lines. Preparatory work is under way as GMRC has engaged Detailed Design Consultants to finalise structural alignments and has begun geotechnical testing, utility diversion planning and tendering to reduce lead time before construction. A direct metro link to the South West Ahmedabad Sports Arena (SWASA) at Godhavi is included to improve access to the developing complex and support potential events related to Gujarat’s bid for the 2030 Commonwealth Games. The PIB clearance marks a significant step while final cabinet approval will determine the course and timing of construction and future extensions towards Dholera. national_raw_news.content: PIB Backgrounder MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026 Certainty and Uniformity in Mineral Taxation प्रविष्टि तिथि: 13 AUG 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi Mineral Regulations: An Overview Minerals are vital natural resources with strong geopolitical importance. They support infrastructure, digital systems, manufacturing, energy security, and national economic growth. Balanced and sustainable mineral development across regions remains a key foundation for advancing public interest and long-term prosperity. In India, mining is governed by the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. For the wider public interest, the Union controls mine regulation and mineral development under Section 2 of the Act. The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 introduces changes in this Act to create a uniform and balanced fiscal framework for the mineral sector nationwide. It restricts State governments from imposing any new taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands without conditions/restrictions prescribed by the Central government. The bill has been passed by both houses of Parliament. Why the Amendment is Needed The MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026 addresses the following challenges arising from the existing framework for taxation and levies in the mining sector: A heavy tax burden on the mining sector. Unpredictable introduction of taxes, cess and other levies, even after mining operations had commenced. Multiple taxes, cess and other levies on the production or dispatch of minerals. Non-uniform rates of taxes and other levies among States. Imposition of taxes, cess or levies with retrospective effect. These challenges have created multiple issues for mining as well as for public interest: Excessive fiscal burden made mining commercially unviable, discouraged mineral extraction and, in some cases, led to closure of mines. Additional and unpredictable costs affected small and medium-scale mining operators disproportionately. High and uneven levies pushed industries to avoid local supply chains. This created weaker markets, higher transport costs, and more pollution. Costlier domestic supply also created a risk of higher mineral imports, despite sufficient local mineral resources. Multiple and inconsistent taxes caused a cascading tax effect and high compliance costs, slowing down economic growth. An excessive tax burden at the extraction stage ultimately raises the cost of goods and services. This increases the cost of living for the common citizen. Retrospective imposition of taxes caused legal uncertainty and eroded investors’ trust. Any fiscal load on mineral extraction must follow a uniform and balanced framework nationwide. Levies should never outweigh mining’s economic value or profitability. The State, as trustee of natural resources, holds responsibility to protect national interest. It must ensure harmonised mineral growth across India, instead of uneven, localised pockets of resource-driven expansion. Union control over mineral-bearing lands: The Union will now also regulate mineral-bearing lands having mineral contents. Such lands will be identified as per parameters prescribed by the Central Government under the MMDR Act. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Removes 12-Minute Advertisement Duration Cap for Television Channels Ad Duration Cap Removed to Enable Fair Competition and Ensure Ease of Doing Business Posted On: 14 AUG 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi The Government has decided to remove the 12-minute advertisement duration cap for television channels. The advertisement duration cap for Television was introduced in the year 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994. Since then, the TV broadcasting sector has undergone significant changes. In 2006, there were only 62 TV channels, compared to more than 900 channels at present. At that time, Cable TV, the main platform for delivering TV channels, was analog and had limited carriage capacity, offering consumers very limited choice. Following the complete digitization of the Cable TV sector, all TV distribution platforms, including DTH, Cable TV, HITS and IPTV, are now digital. These platforms currently carry 300 and 500 channels or more, meeting diverse consumer needs and enabling greater variety. Consequently, there is now adequate competition in market dynamics. In view of the changes that have occurred in the TV broadcasting sector, a need was felt to revisit the stipulations relating to advertisement duration. In India, the sector is heavily dependent on advertising, irrespective of whether a channel is ‘pay’ or ‘free-to-air’. Furthermore, there was a non-level playing field for traditional TV channels vis-à-vis digital media, where no such stipulation on advertisement cap regulation exists. The Ministry of I&B is of the view that there exists adequate competition in the market within the TV industry and between the TV industry and digital media. The Government has decided to remove the advertisement duration cap to enable fair competition and ensure ease of doing business. Sign In Prefer Prefer Proposed Anand Vihar passenger holding area (Pic Via Ministry of Railways/PIB) Indian Railways has accelerated work on passenger holding areas at Anand Vihar Terminal and Udhna Railway Station, with completion targeted before the forthcoming major festival rush. Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reviewed the progress yesterday (14 August) from Rail Bhawan, New Delhi, with Union Minister of State for Railways V Somanna also present. The review focused on expediting ongoing works, addressing site-related challenges and ensuring timely completion of the facilities. It covered civil works, removal of obstructions, utility shifting, structural works, passenger amenities and other associated facilities. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras are to be completed before the forthcoming major festival rush to provide safer, more organised and passenger-centric arrangements. At Anand Vihar Terminal, the facility is being developed in two phases . Phase-I will provide organised space for approximately 4,000 passengers, with work on foundations, plinth beams, structural steel fabrication and other associated activities progressing at a fast pace. Phase-II will further strengthen the facility's passenger-handling capacity, enabling it to accommodate around 7,000 passengers on completion. At Udhna Railway Station, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra is planned to accommodate around 15,000 passengers at a time. Significant progress has already been achieved at site, and after completion, the station will provide improved connectivity between the holding area and the platforms, supporting the orderly movement of passengers and better management of passenger flows. The facilities will provide spacious covered waiting and seating areas, dedicated ticketing facilities, toilets for men and women, drinking water and other essential amenities. Public Address and passenger information systems, CCTV surveillance and security arrangements, adequate lighting, electrical facilities, display boards, signage, organised passenger circulation and furniture are also being provided. The holding areas are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers, helping decongest station platforms, circulating areas and station approaches during peak periods.
